text: {"features":[{"name":"Role-specific motivation","description":"How specifically and convincingly the letter explains why this exact Google Information Security Engineering role is a strong target for the applicant.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"The letter expresses only generic interest in software or security work and gives little reason this particular role stands out."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"The letter shows broad interest in Google, backend work, or security, but its reasons could fit many different engineering roles."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"The letter gives at least one clear role-linked reason for applying, such as security impact, backend work, or scale."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"The letter gives several specific reasons for wanting this role and ties them to the applicant's interests or prior work."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"The letter makes a compelling, individualized case for this exact role by clearly connecting the team's mission to the applicant's career direction and motivations."}]},{"name":"Security automation mission understanding","description":"How well the letter demonstrates understanding that the role centers on automating security processes such as vulnerability handling, triage, variant analysis, and secure-development support.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"The letter treats the job as general software or security work and shows little grasp of its automation-centered mission."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"The letter recognizes a security context but describes the work only at a high level, with little mention of process scaling or response workflows."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"The letter identifies automation of security tasks or vulnerability handling as part of the role, but without much nuance."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"The letter accurately describes several mission elements, such as triage, lifecycle support, scaling expert judgment, or automation for developer teams."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"The letter shows precise role understanding by framing the work as building systems that automate and scale security judgment across vulnerability response and developer workflows."}]},{"name":"Platform leverage orientation","description":"How strongly the letter emphasizes interest in foundational systems whose improvements benefit many teams rather than a single product.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"The letter shows no clear preference for foundational or cross-team engineering work."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"The letter hints at liking broad impact, but the idea stays generic and underdeveloped."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"The letter states interest in work that benefits more than one team or product."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"The letter clearly prefers central platform or foundational infrastructure because of its multiplier effect."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"The letter repeatedly and convincingly frames the applicant's motivation around building foundational systems whose gains propagate across an organization."}]},{"name":"Developer enablement orientation","description":"How strongly the letter focuses on helping other engineers adopt secure practices with less friction.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"The letter does not discuss the needs of downstream developer teams or how tooling should help them."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"The letter mentions helping others in general terms but does not show a concrete enablement mindset."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"The letter notes a desire to make security easier, more routine, or more accessible for engineers."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"The letter emphasizes reducing friction, making secure defaults easy, or returning time to engineers through tooling."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"The letter clearly centers internal developer experience by portraying success as helping busy engineers do the secure thing by default."}]},{"name":"Relevant software experience depth","description":"How much proven production software experience the letter shows through years of work and scope of testing, maintenance, and launches.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"The letter shows only minimal depth beyond the role minimum, typically around 3 years of experience with responsibility for only a small number of production services."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"The letter shows acceptable early-career depth, such as around 3 years with moderate service exposure or around 5 years with limited service exposure."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"The letter shows solid mid-level depth, such as around 5 years with several services or around 7 years with limited service count."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"The letter shows strong depth, such as around 5 years with broad service exposure or around 7 years with several production services."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"The letter shows very strong depth, typically pairing around 7 years of experience with broad responsibility across many production services."}]},{"name":"Degree attainment","description":"How advanced the applicant's formal degree is relative to the role's preferred educational background.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"The highest degree presented is a bachelor's degree in a relevant technical field."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"The highest degree presented is a bachelor's degree, with some additional advanced-study signal beyond the basic degree."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"The highest degree presented is a master's degree in a relevant technical field."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"The highest degree presented is a master's degree, with an added advanced-study or research-oriented signal beyond the degree itself."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"The highest degree presented is a doctoral degree in a relevant technical field."}]},{"name":"Go backend alignment","description":"How strongly the letter establishes Go as a core production language relevant to the backend systems in the role.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"The letter mentions Go only in a résumé-like way, with no further evidence of depth or backend relevance."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"The letter says Go is a regular or primary language but offers little context about what was built with it."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"The letter makes Go sound central to day-to-day work on production services."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"The letter ties Go experience to backend systems or tooling similar to the role's server-side work."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"The letter presents Go as a main production language and explicitly connects it to designing or operating backend infrastructure closely aligned with the role."}]},{"name":"Python depth","description":"How strongly the letter demonstrates production use of Python for services, tooling, automation, or agents relevant to the role.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"The letter does not mention Python or gives no evidence of having used it."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"The letter mentions Python briefly as a secondary language without describing meaningful use."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"The letter states regular Python use for tooling, scripts, prototypes, or internal services."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"The letter shows substantial Python ownership across production services or automation layers."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"The letter portrays Python as a major working language with concrete, production-grade use in services, tooling, or agent frameworks."}]},{"name":"AI application experience","description":"How well the letter shows direct experience building and deploying AI or LLM-based functionality in production.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"The letter gives no evidence of AI or LLM experience."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"The letter mentions AI interest or exposure without concrete shipped work."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"The letter states direct work on model-backed or LLM-enabled features."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"The letter shows shipped AI functionality plus some attention to evaluation, trustworthiness, or failure modes."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"The letter presents substantial production AI experience that combines shipping model-backed features with explicit methods for making them reliable or safe."}]},{"name":"Agentic systems design","description":"How strongly the letter shows experience designing systems where agents operate within deliberate constraints.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"The letter gives no evidence of agentic systems work."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"The letter mentions automation or agents vaguely without describing an architecture."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"The letter states experience building agent-based or agentic tooling."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"The letter describes agentic systems with distinct roles for agents and surrounding control services."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"The letter shows design ownership of agentic architectures, typically specifying Python agents paired with Go services that constrain, log, or audit their actions."}]},{"name":"Vulnerability triage automation","description":"How strongly the letter demonstrates direct experience automating vulnerability intake, classification, routing, or related response workflows.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"The letter gives no evidence of work on vulnerability-handling automation."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"The letter refers to security automation only generally, without a concrete triage example."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"The letter states that the applicant automated vulnerability report intake or triage."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"The letter describes a clear workflow improvement such as classification, routing, deduplication, or prioritization."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"The letter presents concrete ownership of transforming a manual vulnerability queue into a largely automated pipeline and makes the operational benefit clear."}]},{"name":"Security assessment experience","description":"How much hands-on experience the letter shows in assessing systems for security issues.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"The letter gives no evidence of performing security assessments."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"The letter implies security awareness but does not describe actual assessment work."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"The letter states experience with security assessments, reviews, or threat models."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"The letter describes assessments across new designs or existing services and mentions findings, remediation, or both."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"The letter shows strong hands-on assessment experience by presenting it as recurring work that includes threat modeling, code review, documented findings, and follow-through on fixes."}]},{"name":"Algorithmic fluency","description":"How clearly the letter demonstrates strong algorithmic thinking using data structures and algorithms in real systems.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"The letter gives no evidence of algorithmic strength."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"The letter gestures toward technical problem solving but offers no clear data-structure or algorithm example."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"The letter explicitly claims algorithmic strength or gives a basic example of algorithmic improvement."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"The letter provides a concrete example of using better algorithms or structures to improve a production system."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"The letter makes algorithmic skill vivid and current through a strong example that materially changed performance, correctness, or system simplicity."}]},{"name":"Security engineering mindset","description":"How well the letter conveys a rigor-oriented, trust-conscious approach suited to building security-sensitive systems.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"The letter does not articulate any security-specific engineering philosophy or rigor."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"The letter expresses general seriousness about security but without concrete principles."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"The letter shows some mindset cues such as thinking like an attacker, valuing secure defaults, or emphasizing reliability."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"The letter articulates specific security-engineering principles such as trust boundaries, failure modes, guardrails, auditability, or quiet resilience."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"The letter consistently frames past work and future interest around building trustworthy systems to a higher bar, using concrete security-minded principles rather than slogans."}]},{"name":"Security credential strength","description":"How strong the applicant's formal security certification signal is.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"The letter mentions no security certification."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"The letter mentions a security credential in passing but gives little sense of its level or relevance."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"The letter presents an entry-level or foundational security certification as evidence of baseline security knowledge."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"The letter presents a stronger hands-on security certification or equivalent credential but gives limited detail about what it demonstrates."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"The letter presents a strong hands-on credential and explicitly explains it as evidence of practical exploitation or assessment capability."}]},{"name":"Offensive security practice","description":"How much the letter shows ongoing practice in attacker-style security work outside normal development duties.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"The letter gives no evidence of offensive security practice."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"The letter mentions casual or occasional exposure to offensive techniques without showing sustained practice."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"The letter states regular participation in capture-the-flag events or similar offensive practice."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"The letter presents sustained offensive practice as an intentional way to sharpen defensive thinking."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"The letter shows sustained offensive practice with especially strong results, such as recurring high placements or a clearly serious competitive commitment."}]},{"name":"Open-source engagement","description":"How strongly the letter demonstrates contributing to or maintaining open-source software.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"The letter gives no evidence of open-source involvement."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"The letter mentions minor or unspecified open-source interaction without a clear contribution record."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"The letter states occasional upstream patches or contributions when work uncovers defects."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"The letter shows a regular habit of contributing fixes upstream or otherwise improving the open-source tools it depends on."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"The letter shows substantial open-source ownership, such as maintaining a public project with reviews, releases, or an external contributor base."}]},{"name":"Personal project sophistication","description":"How technically ambitious and relevant the letter's side projects are as signals of independent engineering ability.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"The letter gives no side-project example."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"The letter mentions only a small utility or simple app with limited technical challenge."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"The letter describes a modest personal project that shows initiative but limited systems complexity."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"The letter describes a technically substantial project with meaningful systems design or operational complexity."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"The letter describes a highly ambitious side project, often distributed or failure-oriented, that clearly demonstrates deep independent engineering."}]},{"name":"Achievement specificity","description":"How concrete and evidence-based the letter's claims are about accomplishments and skills.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"The letter relies mostly on broad claims and general self-description with little concrete evidence."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"The letter includes a few specific facts such as years or languages but gives little detail on methods, examples, or outcomes."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"The letter provides at least one concrete example of work or improvement relevant to the role."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"The letter supports several claims with distinct examples, technical details, or observable outcomes."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"The letter consistently grounds its claims in vivid, role-relevant examples that show what was built, how it worked, and what changed as a result."}]},{"name":"Structural coherence","description":"How logically organized and easy to follow the letter is as a complete argument for fit.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"The letter reads as disjointed, awkwardly sequenced, or hard to follow as an application narrative."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"The letter has a recognizable structure but a choppy flow, abrupt jumps, or overly fragmentary presentation."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"The letter is generally coherent and readable, though some transitions or emphasis feel formulaic or uneven."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"The letter flows well from motivation to evidence to fit, with clear progression and good paragraph-level organization."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"The letter delivers a highly cohesive narrative in which each paragraph builds naturally toward a strong case for fit."}]},{"name":"Writing mechanics","description":"How cleanly the letter is written at the sentence level, including spelling, grammar, and proofreading.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"The letter contains frequent errors that are immediately noticeable and repeatedly distract from the content."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"The letter contains several noticeable errors that weaken polish but do not obscure meaning."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"The letter contains a few minor errors or awkward phrasings but remains generally polished."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"The letter is cleanly written with only isolated slips, if any."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"The letter is essentially error-free and professionally polished throughout."}]}]}
